stories.headline: Lahore records severe smog as officials dispute sources of cross-border pollution
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 10 November that Lahore ranked as the world's most polluted major city in a live air-quality ranking. Pakistani officials attributed part of the pollution to fireworks across the border after Diwali; this attribution is a claim, not proof that a single source caused the episode.

stories.background: The report highlights severe particulate pollution in Lahore and New Delhi after Diwali. Weather, local emissions and transboundary transport can all affect pollution levels; a live ranking is time-specific.

stories.headline: Pakistan signals push for greater climate finance at COP31
stories.summary: Pakistan's foreign ministry said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would seek increased climate financing for developing countries at COP31 in Türkiye, according to reporting on 10 November. The planned address was scheduled for 11 November and must not be described as already delivered.

stories.headline: Hormuz LNG tanker exits reach post-conflict monthly high in October
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 10 November that 31 laden LNG tankers exited the Strait of Hormuz during October 2026, the highest monthly tally since the conflict disrupted traffic in February. S&P Global Energy data identified 23 tankers from Qatar's Ras Laffan and eight from the UAE's Das Island.

stories.headline: COP31 host Türkiye proposes global electrification target for 2035
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye proposed increasing electricity's share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035, compared with approximately one-fifth currently. Reuters reported concerns that electrification alone will not guarantee lower emissions unless power generation becomes cleaner.

stories.background: The proposal remained under discussion on 10 November, not an adopted final COP agreement. Electrification can lower fossil-fuel use in transport and heating, but emissions benefits depend on the electricity mix.
